title: Stochastic mash-up optimizer: run it on a score, it finds clips to mash in and proposes candidates worth rating
description:
Run on a Score; it searches the library for clips to mash in, in many ways (region, warp/speed/repitch/reverse, transposition from the compiler's auto fit, role, entry, processing), scores them without rendering via a compile-informed surrogate (apricity compile's warp maps, semitones and gains applied to per-beat manifest features), explores with a seeded MAP-Elites archive (role x register x rhythm x source family) plus an analytic gain step, then a render ladder (48 + null at 8 bars -> 12 -> 4 full) to 3 diverse finalists + the incumbent for a listening cycle (apricitus-2101dd). Objective: clash, busyness, masking, chord fit, rhythm, artefacts, taste, and a positive contribution term vs a null 'no new part' control (margin 2). Human verdicts calibrate weights (Bradley-Terry, >= 20 pairs, capped).

User decisions (2026-09-27): add a new part by default, re-cast an existing role as an option; Phase 1 tries ALL roles at once (loop, bass, pad, stab, chop, sliced riff); key/progression change only as a separately requested cycle type; CLAP audio embeddings in Phase 1 (genre/timbre fit is the checker's biggest blind spot); non-semitone repitch allowed only if the finalist lands within 8 cents of 12-TET.

Design: Fable spec (full text in the first comment). Evidence: the compile-informed per-beat proxy matches rendered stems at median chroma cosine 0.92/0.96 and ranks per-beat clash with Spearman 0.57 (pair) / 0.69 (chord) on Ave House (33 beats; re-run and confirmed). Candidate-level rho is the Phase 1 gate.

comments.text:
# Stochastic mash-up optimizer for Apricity (design, 2026-09-27)

Builds on `spec-checker.md` (the rendered harmony checker) and `spec-layer.md` (the layer
validator). Neither is repeated here; where this spec changes them it says so.

**One sentence:** for a score S, a seeded search proposes "mash clip X into S in way G", scores
tens of thousands of proposals in milliseconds from manifests plus the compiler's own timeline,
renders the ~150 that survive, and hands the human 3 diverse finalists plus "keep as it was";
the verdicts move the weights.

## 0. What I verified (this machine, read-only)

| Fact | Measured | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `apricity compile` on Ave House | < 10 ms; gives per event `src_start/src_end`, a `warp` map (source seconds -> event beats), `semitones`, `tuning_cents`, `gain_db`, `mode`; per track `stretch`, `beat_ratio`, `level_db`, effects, automation points; per chord span the solver's `voices` (semitones, on_chord, off_key, runners-up) | The surrogate must not guess the transposition or the stretch: the compiler tells it for free. Explorer v0's proxy (rho -0.16) ignored exactly this. |
| Full render with `--stems` + `check-stems.py` | 16.4 s + 6.3 s = 23 s (9 stems, 40 bars) | Full-fidelity eval cost. |
| 8-bar render (`--bars 9-16`) + check | 3.6 s + 2.0 s = 5.6 s | Mid-fidelity eval cost; 4 workers give ~40/min. |
| Manifests | 148; 124 with `tonal.beat_chroma` (per beat, 12 pcs, max-normalized) and `rhythm.beat_loudness` (dB); `notes` in 128; saved clips: 430 loop, 355 hold, 572 sec, 497 shot, 1125 phrase; 62 samples at 90-130 bpm | Per-beat chroma and loudness already exist. Missing: per-beat band energy, onsets, tonalness, flatness, embeddings. |
| Proxy probe (`scratchpad/opt/proxy_probe.py`) | Manifest `beat_chroma`, windowed by the compiled warp map and rolled by the compiled `semitones`, vs the rendered stems' per-beat chroma: median cosine 0.92 (dark) / 0.96 (bright). Per-beat pair-clash Spearman 0.57, chord-clash 0.69 (33 beats where both sound; small n, one score) | The compile-informed surrogate is feasible. The rendered stems include hp 180 and EQ notches the proxy did not model, and it still tracks. Candidate-level rho is **unverified** (Phase 1 acceptance test). |
| Library | 108 Ratings (92 clip, 12 score, 4 sample); 0 ListeningCycle / CycleVerdict; the `cycle publish/pull` runner from apricitus-2101dd does not exist in code yet (grep: nothing in scripts/, analysis/, web/src, crates/) | Feedback today is `renders/log.jsonl` (17 lines, 5 A/B pairs) plus the Listening Room artifact. |
| Hardware | 10 cores, 32 GB | Budgets below assume 4 render workers (the build-concurrency memory rule is about cargo, not renders, but 4 keeps the laptop usable). |

## 1. The search space: the genome

A candidate is `(S, X, G)`: the incumbent score S (fixed text), a source sample X, and a genome G
that becomes **one `clip` line plus one `track` block** appended to S (Phase 1) or a rewrite of
an existing role (the explorer's `cast.swap`). The genome is the union of what the language can
express for one part; each gene lists its domain and whether it is discrete (D) or continuous (C).

| Gene | Domain | D/C | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | sample path, from the licensed pool (ccMixter CC BY/BY-SA, LoC, citizen-dj, marine-band; **no ND/NC**, reuse `candidates._license_ok`) with `beat_chroma` present | D (~120) | Drum kits and one-shots are sources only for the `stab`/`chop` roles. |
| `region` | a saved clip (`loop-N`, `hold-N`, `sec-XN`, `phrase-N`, `shot-N`), or `beats a..b` with `a` on the sample's bar grid and `b-a` in {4, 8, 16, 32} sample beats, or `pick <n>bars` (compiler-chosen, the baseline) | D | Saved clips first (~2,000 usable); the bar-grid form makes every bar of every sample reachable (~10x more). |
| `ratio` | auto (compiler: least stretch of 1/2, 1, 2) / 0.5 / 1 / 2 | D | With `half`/`double`/`speed` on the track this is the time transform. Gate: resulting stretch in [0.67, 1.5] (`beats`), [0.8, 1.25] (others), as in spec-layer. |
| `speed` (track) | 0.5-2, log-uniform, or {0.5, 1, 2} | C (quantized to D in Phase 1) | Pitch-preserving. |
| `warp` | complex / beats / texture / repitch | D | `repitch` couples pitch to `speed` (12·log2 speed semitones): it is the "play it like a record" dimension the user asked about; it also exempts the clip from the solver. |
| `repitch_speed` | 0.5-2 log-uniform, plus the 12-TET grid 2^(k/12) | C, with a D grid | Only when `warp repitch`. Semitone-grid values are the musically safe ones; the continuous ones are the interesting ones (a 5th up at 1.5x etc.). |
| `reverse` | bool | D | |
| `transpose` | auto / follow / n in [-12, 12] | D | `auto` = the compiler's solver, and it is **always the baseline gene value**: the genome only overrides when the surrogate says a fixed shift beats the solver's (which optimizes fit per chord, not clash against the stack). |
| `role_hint` | any / root / third / fifth / seventh / bass / chord | D | The solver's hint. |
| `root_pin` | none / pitch class x octave | D (12 x 4) | Corrects mis-heard roots (the Ab1 story); also required for pitched tracks. |
| `role` | loop / bass / pad / stab / chop / riff | D | Decides the track shape (below) and the objective's role weights. |
| pitched shape (`bass`, `stab`, `pad` from a `hold`/`shot`) | `voicing` root/power/triad/seventh; `octave` 1-5; `steps` from a small pattern bank (one note a bar, on-beats, off-beats, 2-bar rhythm); `attack` 0-300 ms, `release` 50-2000 ms (log) | D except attack/release (C) | This is where **the platform's pitch-shifting is leveraged**: one hold becomes a bass line or a chord pad at exact chord tones. |
| `chop` shape | a `kit` `slice ... by beats 0.5 | by transients`, a `steps` pattern over slice numbers from a bank plus mutation (swap two slices, drop one, repeat one) | D, combinatorial | Phase 3; the sliced riff is the biggest creative dimension and the busiest, so it needs the density term first. |
| `entry` | a bars range from the score's **section grid** (Ave House: 1-8, 9-24, 25-32, 33-40, and unions), plus `every <n>bars` / `at` from a bank | D | The new part enters where the arrangement has room; sections are read from the incumbent's automation and `bars` ranges, else 8-bar blocks. |
| `volume` | -18..+3 dB | C | Capped above so loudness cannot buy contribution. |
| `hp`, `lp` | 20-2000 Hz / 800-20000 Hz, log; off | C (+ off) | |
| `notches` | up to 3 (Hz from the notch finder, gain in {-4,-6,-8,-10}, q in {8,12}) | D | Reuse `ops.track_eq_notch`. |
| `send plate` | 0-50 % | C | The only send in Ave House; read the sends from S. |
| `group` | the group the incumbent's music uses, or master | D | So the breakdown filter and pump apply to the new part. |
| `song_key`, `progression` | 24 keys x mode; substitutions from a bank (relative, parallel, a borrowed iv, a ii-V) | D | **Not searched without asking.** Offered as a separate "question" (see 5); Phase 3. |

Sizes: the discrete core (source x saved region x ratio x transpose-mode x role x entry) is
about 2,000 x 3 x 4 x 3 x 3 ~ 200k for Ave House with saved clips only; the surrogate can
score all of it (2 ms each ~ 7 min single-threaded, or sample 50k in ~2 min). The continuous
genes are few (<= 8 per candidate) and are handled by the analytic gain step and a small ES
at render fidelity, not by the surrogate's enumeration.

Encoding: a JSON dict (`genome.json`) with the gene names above; `genome.to_ops()` yields typed
ops (the existing `ops.py` set plus new ones in 6) applied to S's text; `genome.text(S)` is the
candidate score. The dict is the unit that is hashed, cached, logged and mutated.

## 2. The surrogate (no rendering)

### 2a. How it works
1. `apricity compile` the candidate text (< 10 ms). Read: every event's source, `src_start`,
   `src_end`, `warp`, `semitones`, `gain_db`, `mode`; every track's automation; every span's chord
   tones and the solver's `voices`.
2. For each event and each score beat b it covers: `t = interp(b + 0.5, warp[:,1], warp[:,0])`
   gives the source time; the manifest beat index `i = searchsorted(beats, t) - 1`. Read the
   per-beat features at `i` (the region is a window of per-beat analysis; stretch only changes
   which `i` each `b` maps to, and a `ratio 2` reads two source beats per score beat: average
   them).
3. Analytic transforms:
   - transposition rotates chroma (`np.roll(chroma, semitones)`) and shifts the band-energy
     vector by `semitones/12 * bands_per_octave` with linear interpolation (24 log bands over
     20 Hz-16 kHz is 2.49 bands per octave);
   - stretch (`complex`/`beats`/`texture`) preserves pitch content: no change to chroma or bands;
   - `repitch` does both (`12*log2(speed)` semitones, and time by `1/speed`);
   - `reverse` mirrors the window (chroma per beat is unchanged; onsets mirror);
   - gain, `volume` and the level match multiply (`10^(dB/20)`); track and group **automation**
     becomes a per-beat gain envelope from the compiled points (linear or step) — the probe
     skipped this and lost `dark`'s bars 9-24 (its volume automation mutes it); it must be in;
   - `hp`/`lp`/`eq` multiply the band vector by the filter's magnitude response sampled at band
     centres; chroma is corrected by removing the mass of transcribed `notes` whose MIDI pitch
     falls below the hp (or above the lp) cutoff (approximate, but it makes an hp 180 stop the
     bass flag, which is what the checker sees);
   - pitched tracks (`voicing`, `notes`): synthesize the chroma per beat from the chord tones the
     compiler already resolved (the event's `semitones` per note), weighted by the hold's
     tonalness; bands shift as above.
4. Build the per-beat stack vectors for S's existing tracks the same way (cached per S), then
   evaluate every objective term of section 4 that has a manifest form: clash (the kernel from
   `check.py`, verbatim), chord/key fit, masking (band cosine), rhythmic interlock (onset
   envelopes), density, contribution, artefacts, taste prior. The surrogate returns the same term
   vector as the rendered validator, so calibration compares like with like.

Cost: per candidate, ~64-160 beats x (12-dim kernel + 24-band ops) in numpy; batched over
candidates sharing a source it is ~1-2 ms each (target: >= 500 candidates/s single-threaded;
verify in Phase 1).

### 2b. Per-beat features to precompute (fit profiles)
Stored in a sidecar `samples/<path>.apricity.features.npz` keyed by the manifest's `source.sha256`
(so `apricity analyze` re-runs invalidate it), with a small per-clip summary (the fit profile of
apricitus-1dc58b) written into the manifest's `annotations.clips[*].fit`. The sidecar, per sample:

| Array | Shape | Have today? |
|---|---|---|
| `beat_chroma` | (beats, 12), HPSS-harmonic HPCP, max-normalized | yes (manifest) |
| `beat_loudness` | (beats,) dB | yes (manifest) |
| `beat_tonalness` | (beats,) 1 - spectral flatness of the harmonic part | **no** |
| `beat_bands` | (beats*4, 24) log-band energy on a quarter-beat grid, the layer.py filterbank | **no** |
| `beat_onsets` | (beats*4,) onset strength on the quarter-beat grid, plus `onset_count` per beat | **no** |
| `beat_bass_share` | (beats,) energy below 150 Hz / total | **no** (notes approximate it) |
| `embedding` | (512,) CLAP audio embedding per saved clip (and per 8-bar window) | **no** (Phase 3) |
| per clip `fit`: best key + off-key share, semitone smear, bass share, percussive share, tonalness, tempo | dict | **no** (apricitus-1dc58b's spec) |

Cost: one STFT pass per sample in the analysis venv (librosa 1.0, essentia present):
~1-3 s per 3-minute sample, ~5 minutes for the library; ~50 KB float16 per sample, ~8 MB total.
The 24 manifests without `beat_chroma` (short hits) get the sidecar only if they are longer
than 2 beats; shots use their whole-clip vectors.

### 2c. Calibration
- Against the rendered validator: every optimizer run renders its survivors (8-bar stems +
  `check-layer`) and logs `(surrogate terms, rendered terms)` per candidate to
  `renders/optimize/calibration.jsonl`. Report Spearman rho per term and on the composite, and
  recall@12 (how many of the rendered top 4 the surrogate ranked in its top 12). **Target rho >=
  0.6 on the composite over >= 48 candidates; recall@12 >= 0.75.** If a term's rho < 0.3 it is
  dropped from the surrogate's screen (kept at render) until fixed; the notebook says so.
- Fit a per-term linear correction (`rendered ~ a + b*surrogate`) by least squares once >= 100
  pairs exist; the surrogate's job is ranking, so the correction only matters for the null margin.
- Against humans: the surrogate is never fit to humans directly; the weights over terms are
  (section 5), and they apply to both fidelities.

## 3. The optimizer

### 3a. Options considered
| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Real gradients / CMA-ES over all knobs | Most of the genome is discrete (source, region, mode, role, entry); gradients only exist in the surrogate's gains. Use them there (3b step 2), nowhere else. |
| Simulated annealing / a single (1+lambda)-ES | Cheap and seedable, but one chain converges on one basin; the user wants **three different ideas**, not three tweaks of one (apricitus-49aa1b comment). |
| Bandit over sources (Thompson / UCB) | Right tool for the **overnight** loop: sources are arms, the rendered-vs-null gain is the reward, and the human's pick is the strongest reward. Adopted for run-to-run, not within a cycle. |
| Multi-fidelity successive halving | Already in explorer v0 and it worked mechanically; keep it as the fidelity ladder. |
| MAP-Elites (quality-diversity) | Gives a diverse elite set for free, one per behaviour cell, which is exactly the finalist requirement, and it is trivially seedable. Adopted as the archive. |

### 3b. Recommended architecture: MAP-Elites over a compile-informed surrogate, with a render ladder

```
seed -> priors -> [L0 surrogate, 50k]  -> archive of elites (cells)
                    -> analytic gain step per elite (hp/volume/notch from the surrogate's gradient)
     -> [L1 8-bar render + check-layer, 48 + null] -> successive halving -> [L1, 12 x 6 ES evals]
     -> [L2 full render + check, 3 + incumbent]     -> MMR finalists -> cycle folder
```

- **Seeding and reproducibility.** One `--seed`; `numpy.random.default_rng(seed)` drives every
  choice; candidates are evaluated in sorted genome-hash order so worker scheduling cannot change
  results; the render cache is keyed by score sha (existing). Same seed + same library sha set =>
  identical `notebook.jsonl` up to timestamps (an acceptance test).
- **L0, surrogate (2 min).** Sample 50k genomes: source from the bandit prior (uniform on the
  first run), region uniform over saved clips (Phase 1) and bar-grid windows (Phase 2), ratio
  from the stretch gate, transpose auto with p=0.6 else follow/fixed, role from the score's
  **role gap** (which roles the stack lacks: Ave House lacks pad, stab, chop), entry uniform over
  sections. Evaluate; insert into a **MAP-Elites archive** whose cells are
  `role (6) x register (bass/mid/high from bass share and centroid, 3) x rhythmic class
  (sustained / sparse / busy from onset count per bar, 3) x source family (ccMixter / LoC /
  citizen-dj / marine-band / kit, 5)` = 270 cells; each cell keeps its top 2 by composite.
  Then 20 rounds of 2k **mutations** of random elites (change one gene: neighbour region,
  +-1 ratio step, transpose +-1/+-12, role hint, entry, warp mode; crossover between two elites of
  the same role) — this is where the "stochastic" part earns its keep, reaching bar-grid regions
  and repitch speeds that uniform sampling misses.
- **Analytic gain step.** For each elite, minimize the surrogate composite over the continuous
  gains (volume, hp cutoff, up to 3 notch gains, send) with `scipy.optimize.minimize` (L-BFGS-B,
  bounds from the genome table, <= 50 iterations, ~10 ms): the clash and masking terms are
  smooth in per-band gains, so this is the "gradient descent" the user asked for, applied where
  it exists.
- **L1, 8-bar render (~5.6 s each, 4 workers).** Take the archive's best 48 by composite subject
  to at most 2 per source and at least 1 per non-empty role; render each on the score's
  **train window** (the section it enters; for a part spanning sections, the first 8 bars), with
  `--stems`; run `check-layer` with **the null control** (the stack alone, same window, same
  terms) in the same batch. ~70 s wall. Successive halving: keep 12 (distinct sources, at
  least one per role that beats the null); for each run a **(1+1)-ES with 6 evals** over the
  continuous genes at L1 (step sizes: 2 dB, 1/3 octave, 10 % send; accept on train-window gain
  >= 0.5 with the holdout window not dropping, the explorer's rule). ~2 min. Then keep 4.
- **L2, full render (23 s each).** The 4 plus the incumbent (and the incumbent twice, the
  determinism control). ~2.5 min with 4 workers.
- **Finalists.** MMR over the 4 (section 5) to 3 + keep.

Budget per cycle on this laptop: ~50k surrogate evals (2 min), 48 + 72 = 120 L1 renders (~3.5
min), 6 L2 renders (~2.5 min), overhead (compile, features) ~1 min: **about 10 minutes**, and the
user is only asked once. An **overnight** run repeats cycles with new seeds and roles; between
cycles the source bandit (Beta posterior on "beat the null at L1") and the role gap update the
priors; each cycle leaves its own finalist folder, and the morning report ranks cycles by their
best rendered margin over the null. 8 hours ~ 40 cycles ~ 5,000 renders ~ 2M surrogate evals.

Why one archive and not a beam: the archive's cells are the diversity contract, and it is the
same object the finalist picker reads; a beam would need a separate diversity rule anyway.

## 4. Objective terms

Composite `J = 100 * (1 - sum_k w_k * p_k / sum_k w_k) + w_c * contribution`, terms in [0, 1];
penalties `p_k`, one positive term. Rendered and surrogate versions share definitions. Defaults
(before any human data), and how each is computed:

| Term | w | Definition | Anti-gaming |
|---|---|---|---|
| clash | 0.30 | `check.py`'s pair + chord + bass-root kernel, per beat, loudness-weighted, only where the candidate sounds | unchanged from spec-checker; no mute/delete ops exist |
| chord fit | 0.10 | 1 - the solver's `on_chord` for the candidate's voice, from `compile` (surrogate) or the rendered on-chord share (render) | |
| masking | 0.15 | tonalness-weighted cosine of the candidate's band vector against each stack stem's, per beat; plus a register penalty when the candidate's centroid sits within 1/3 octave of a stack stem's for > 50 % of beats | level-matched first |
| rhythmic interlock | 0.10 | onset-envelope correlation with the stack at lag 0: r > 0.6 penalized (doubling); off-grid onsets (> 30 ms from the quarter-beat grid) penalized; a small reward (<= 0.3 of the term) for onsets in the stack's quiet quarter-beat slots | reward capped, pads exempt |
| density / busyness | 0.15 | mix onset count per bar after adding the part vs the incumbent's: penalty grows linearly from +25 % to +60 % (=1); plus the candidate's own onsets per bar > 8 (=1 at 16), and spectral-flux increase of the mix > 30 %. **The user dislikes busy: this is the second-heaviest term.** | computed on the mix, so a quiet part still counts if it fills every gap |
| artefacts | 0.05 | `|log2 stretch|/1`, `|semitones|/7`, `|log2 repitch_speed|/1`, flatness increase (render only) | |
| energy / guards | gate | spec-checker's energy, density, coverage, tuning guards, and spec-layer's silent, double, stretch, tuning gates | hard gates |
| **contribution** (positive) | 0.20 | max over three channels, each in [0,1]: (a) **band fill**: energy the part adds in bands where the stack is > 24 dB below its own loudest band (weighted by how much of the piece those bands stay empty); (b) **harmonic addition**: chord tones the part supplies that the stack's coverage lacks (from the solver's `coverage`, Ave House's VII bar sits at 38 %); (c) **motion**: the mix's bar-to-bar band-energy variance rises by 10-40 % (0 outside that range, so more motion is not always better) | the null control has contribution 0 and every penalty 0: a candidate is offered only if `J - J_null >= delta`, delta = 2 points, raised when the human keeps picking "keep" (5) |
| taste prior | 0.10 | 1 - (the clip's or sample's star rating / 4) when rated, 0.5 when not; Phase 3 adds the CLAP taste probe | never above 0.15, so an unrated clip can still win |

Timbre/genre fit and the embedding question: CLAP (laion-clap; torch 2.14 is installed, the
package and its ~600 MB checkpoint are not) gives one 512-d vector per clip in ~50 ms on CPU;
OpenL3 is the fallback. The whole library is 3k clips: a numpy cosine over a (3000, 512) matrix
is microseconds. **A DynamoDB vector index does not help here**: the search runs locally, the
embeddings fit in one npz, and the cloud side only rates. It would matter if the library grew
to 100k+ clips or if the web app got a "find clips like this" feature; keep it as that
feature's design, not the optimizer's. What CLAP is for: (1) a **taste probe**: a logistic
regression on embeddings of 4-5 star vs 1-2 star rated clips (92 clip ratings today; a probe
needs ~40 per class to be trusted, so start as a tie-breaker only), (2) a text prompt prior
("smooth deep house pad", "old Moby sample") as a cell-level prior in L0, (3) the diversity
distance in MMR.

## 5. Selecting what the human hears, and feeding verdicts back

- **Finalists.** From the L2 four, greedy MMR: the best first, then the candidate maximizing
  `J - lambda * max_sim(chosen)` with `lambda = 0.5` and similarity = cosine over
  `[term vector, archive-cell one-hot, CLAP embedding]`; hard rules: distinct sources, at most
  one per archive cell, at least one that is not the same role as the previous cycle's winner.
  Plus the incumbent as "keep". Every finalist beats the null by delta; if fewer than 3 do,
  the cycle offers fewer (and says so) rather than padding.
- **What is logged per cycle** (`cycle.json` + `notebook.jsonl`): each option's genome, term
  vector at L1 and L2, `J`, `J_null`, attribution, seed, archive cell, and the surrogate/rendered
  rho of the run.
- **Verdicts -> pairs.** The web page's stars and best-pick become pairs: best beats every other
  option; keep vs each candidate; star gaps of >= 2 between candidates. Appended to
  `renders/log.jsonl` as `ab-pair` (existing shape) with both term vectors.
- **Preference learning.** Bradley-Terry / logistic regression on **term-difference vectors**:
  `P(A > B) = sigma(w . (t_A - t_B))`, with an L2 prior centred on the default weights
  (`lambda = 1/n_pairs`), fit only at >= 20 pairs, weights clipped to [0, 3x default], and at
  most a 25 % move per cycle. Report leave-one-cycle-out agreement; **weights change only if
  agreement with the new weights >= agreement with the old on held-out cycles**. With 5 pairs
  today nothing moves: the defaults stand and the log grows.
- **The null margin.** If "keep" wins 2 cycles in a row, `delta += 1` and the contribution weight
  goes up one step (0.20 -> 0.25); if a candidate wins, `delta` relaxes by 0.5 (floor 2).
- **Source bandit.** Each source keeps a Beta(a, b): +1 a when a candidate from it beats the
  null at L1, +3 when it is picked by the human, +1 b when it loses to the null. Thompson
  sampling picks the L0 source mix on later runs. This is the only place a handful of ratings
  has a large effect, and it only reorders where the search looks, never what wins.

## 6. How it plugs in, and the output

Reuse: `explore/ops.py` (typed, idempotent text ops; fix apricitus-ab3291 first: options must
land before a trailing `#`), `explore/evaluate.py` (sha cache, process pool, shared baseline),
`explore/notebook.py`, `explore/candidates.py` (license filter; extend to holds/shots/secs and
all folders), `check.py` (kernel, guards, `load_stems`), `layer.py` (features, gates, terms,
sidecar cache), `explore/search.py`'s `accept_candidate` and `diverse_top_n`, `scripts/explore.py`'s
candidate file format.

New modules under `analysis/apricity_analyze/explore/`:
- `genome.py`: the dataclass of section 1, `sample(rng, priors)`, `mutate`, `crossover`,
  `to_ops`, `text(S)`, `cell()`.
- `features.py` + `scripts/fit-features.py`: the sidecar of 2b and the manifest `fit` summary;
  `--refresh` recomputes stale shas only.
- `surrogate.py`: `compile_timeline(text)`, `stack_vectors(S)` (cached), `candidate_vectors`,
  `terms(...)`, `gain_step(...)`.
- `objective.py`: the terms and weights of section 4 for both fidelities, `null_control`,
  `composite`; weights read from `renders/optimize/weights.json` (defaults when absent).
- `archive.py`: MAP-Elites (cells, insert, elites, mutation rounds).
- `calibrate.py`: rho / recall@12 per run; Bradley-Terry on `renders/log.jsonl`; writes
  `weights.json` only under the rule in 5.
- `scripts/optimize.py SCORE [--roles pad,bass] [--seed N] [--cycles N] [--workers 4]
  [--budget-l0 50000] [--budget-l1 48]`.
- New ops in `ops.py`: `track.add` (a `clip` line + a `track` block from a genome), `clip.region`,

Scope: roles `pad` and `bass` (holds via `voicing`, `octave`), `loop` (loops/secs); region =
saved clips only; ratio auto/0.5/2; transpose auto/follow/fixed; entry = one section; continuous
genes: volume and hp only (the analytic gain step over those two); surrogate terms: clash, chord
fit, density (from the manifest's onsets proxy: `notes` onset count per beat, an approximation
until 2b lands), taste prior, contribution channel (b) only (from the solver's coverage). No
sidecar yet; no bands, no masking at L0 (masking still runs at L1 via `layer.py`). Archive
cells: role x register x source family. L1 = 48 + null, L2 = 4 + incumbent x2.
Acceptance (all logged in the notebook):
1. Reproducible: two runs with `--seed 7` produce identical `cycle.json` option genomes and
   identical L1/L2 objectives (the render determinism control already exists).
2. Surrogate composite vs `check-layer` composite over the 48 L1 candidates: **Spearman rho >=
   0.6; recall@12 of the rendered top 4 >= 0.75** (on Ave House, roles pad and bass; report
   both roles separately).
3. The null control is a row in the L1 table; no finalist has `J - J_null < 2`.
4. Positive controls: (a) injecting the incumbent's own bright loop as a `loop` candidate ranks

5. Wall time <= 15 min per cycle on this laptop with 4 workers; L0 >= 500 evals/s.
6. `cycle.json` + A-D.m4a are produced and load in the Listening Room artifact.

## 8. Risks

- **The surrogate stays under rho 0.6 at candidate level.** The probe is per beat on one score;
  candidate ranking compounds region choice, level match and automation. Mitigation: Phase 1's
  acceptance test is exactly this number; if it fails, L1's budget rises (96 renders, ~10 more
  minutes) and the surrogate is demoted to a diversity sampler until it passes.
- **Positive terms get gamed** (a loud, wide pad "fills" every band). Mitigation: level match,
  the +3 dB cap, contribution as a max not a sum, the density term on the mix, the null margin.
- **Too few human pairs for learning.** 5 today; a cycle yields ~4-6. Mitigation: the prior-
  centred fit, the held-out agreement rule, and the bandit (which only steers search).
- **Busyness is exactly what quality-diversity rewards** (a "busy" cell always exists).
  Mitigation: the rhythmic-class axis has a "busy" cell but the density term keeps its J low;
  finalists must beat the null, so an empty busy cell is a valid outcome.
- **Render time creep with more stems per candidate.** Ave House is 9 stems; a chop adds a kit.
  Mitigation: L1 renders only the candidate's window; the stack's stems are rendered once per
  run (`layer.py`'s stack cache) and the candidate is rendered alone against them.

## 9. Open questions for the user (with recommended answers)

1. **May the optimizer add a new track to the score, or only re-cast existing roles?** Recommend
   both, with "add a part" as the default (it is what "mash another clip in" means) and
   `--role <existing>` for the explorer's swap.
2. **Which roles first?** Recommend pad and bass for Ave House (the stack has none in the
   breakdown, and the layer slice showed the user rejected pads: the null control and the
   contribution term are what changed), then stabs; chops last, after the density term is
   proven.
3. **Is `warp repitch` at non-semitone speeds allowed in finalists** (a clip a quarter-tone off
   the score, retuned by the detune pass only if the compiler applies it to repitch)? Recommend
   yes at L0/L1 but a finalist must sit within 8 cents of 12-TET after the compiler's retune
   (the tuning guard already enforces this at render), so odd speeds survive only when they
   land near a semitone.
4. **May a cycle change the song's key or progression?** Recommend no by default; offer it as
   its own question type ("same part, three progressions") that the user asks for explicitly,
   since it invalidates every earlier verdict's context.
5. **CLAP now or later?** Recommend later (Phase 3): one ~600 MB download and a new dependency
   for a tie-breaker; the first two phases need the rendered terms and the null control to work
   first, and 92 clip ratings are too few to train a taste probe worth trusting.
